# Using Drovr

<SUBAGENT-STOP>
If you were dispatched as a subagent to execute a specific task, ignore this
reflex — it is for the human-facing agent, not for you. Do your task.
</SUBAGENT-STOP>

## What this is

This is your **always-on router**. Drovr is a working **discipline**, not just an
orchestration engine, and it is your default operating mode. This skill does not
do the work — it tells you *how* to work and *when* a task has outgrown one
context and must become its own phase.

Drovr exists because model output degrades as a context window fills (Chroma's
*context rot*, trychroma.com/research/context-rot). A fresh, tight context beats
a long one. Everything below serves that.

## The principle (always)

**Single writer, read-only explorers.** One agent edits at a time. Fan-out
investigation goes to read-only explorers (e.g. `explore-mcp`), never to parallel
writers. This holds whether you stay inline or escalate to phases.

**Always review.** Any change you write gets reviewed before you call it done —
invoke **`drovr:code-review`** (read-only review subagents; they find, you fix).
This is not optional and not gated on the change's size; it runs whether you
worked inline or across phases.

## For the task in front of you, apply the right methodology skill

Pick by what you are doing — invoke it via the `Skill` tool before you act:

- Implementing a feature or bugfix → **`drovr:tdd`** (test-first, watch it fail).
- Chasing a bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior → **`drovr:systematic-debugging`**.
- About to claim something is done/fixed/passing → **`drovr:verification-before-completion`**.
- Reviewing an artifact (code, spec, plan) → **`drovr:code-review`**. Per the
  *Always review* rule above, this runs on every change — not only before shipping.

## Escalation contract — inline first

**Default: do the work inline in this session.** Do not reach for phases for a
task that fits. Escalate only when a single context cannot hold the work well.

- **Primary signal — context fullness.** If the transcript is filling to the
  point where output would rot, escalate.
- **Secondary heuristic** (a proxy for the above, not a hard rule): roughly
  **10+ files** touched, or **3+ independent work items**.

When you must escalate, pick the smallest tool that fits:

- **Mid-flight escape hatch — author a HANDOFF yourself.** You are deep in a task
  and this context is filling. You have the whole session in context, so compress
  it *yourself*: write a `HANDOFF.md` (the 7-section shape from `drovr:handoff`,
  git pointers included), then continue in a fresh agent seeded from it. Nothing
  compresses it for you — the finishing agent always authors its own handoff.
- **A single planned boundary → `drovr:handoff`.** Hand finished work across one
  phase boundary to a fresh clean-context agent.
- **A full gated run → `drovr:pipeline`.** Brainstorm → plan → implement → review
  with a human approval gate on `spec.md` before any code is written.

**Putting *any* spec/design in front of a human for approval — even a one-off, not a
full pipeline — goes through the review gate, and the gate has two halves you must run
together:** `drovr review summary <run> "<what changed>"` to present `spec.md`, **and** a
backgrounded `drovr review wait <run>` — the *watch*. (The server itself is global and
always-on: `drovr serve` takes **no** run argument and auto-starts on demand, so serving is not
a step you perform per run.) `summary` opens the gate and prints the reviewer's page URL plus
the exact watch command; it does **not** start the watch. Without the watch you never learn the
decision and fall back to hand-polling `GET /state` (the anti-pattern).
`review wait` blocks on the gate and the harness wakes you when the reviewer acts
(exit `0` approved · `3` request-changes + `feedback.json` · `5` cancelled — the human
abandoned the run, stop · `2` timeout, re-run · `1` error, which is **never** an approval).
Revise loop: edit `spec.md` →
`drovr review summary <run> "<what changed>"` → re-background `review wait`. Full mechanics
(state machine, diff baselining, gotchas) live in `drovr:pipeline` → "The spec gate".

**REQUIRED BACKGROUND:** the downstream skills assume this file's contracts —
single-writer rule, the run dir at `~/.local/share/drovr/runs/<name>/`, and that
**drovr composes every brief; you supply only context.** `drovr phase start <run>
<phase> --context "<what this phase needs that drovr cannot know>"` composes the
phase's brief and injects it. Never write the frame yourself: `drovr phase brief`
prints what an agent will be told, and `drovr code-review brief … --angle <angle>`
does the same for a reviewer you spawn in-harness. `phase send` remains for
free-form nudges — a message is not a brief.
</EXTREMELY_IMPORTANT>",
    "hookEventName": "SessionStart"
  }
}

content.text:
`fj auth login` isn't erroring — it's **hanging silently**, and the cause is past the part your dotfiles control.

## What works (ruled out)

1. **`client_ids` wiring is correct.** strace shows fj opening `/home/sauyon/.config/forgejo-cli/client_ids` → the nix store file, successfully. Commit `38b9b17` did its job. fj 0.6.0 only ever checks two paths (`<config>/client_ids`, `/etc/fj/client_ids`) — you hit the right one.
2. **Server side is fine.** `GET /login/oauth/authorize?client_id=23d7b03d-…` returns `303 → /user/login` through Cloudflare. No challenge, no block, `redirect_to` cookie set correctly.

## What actually happens

```
$ fj auth login -H forge.ko.ag
Could not find keys file. Creating a new file.
   ← hangs here forever
```

It hands the authorize URL to `xdg-open` and blocks on its callback listener at `http://127.0.0.1:26218/`. **It never prints the URL to the terminal.** If the browser leg fails or you approve and the redirect doesn't land, you get an infinite silent hang with no error text. No login has ever completed — `~/.local/share/forgejo-cli/` doesn't exist at all.

## Three candidates I can't test without your login

All are on the app registration at `forge.ko.ag/user/settings/applications`:

1. client_id `23d7b03d-a351-4ac2-8d84-53fb9a8ce945` isn't actually registered → "Client ID not found" after you log in
2. Redirect URI isn't exactly `http://127.0.0.1:26218/` — trailing slash is significant
3. **Confidential Client is ON** → token exchange dies with `invalid_client`, because fj sends PKCE with no secret

## Recommendation: skip OAuth entirely

`fj auth add-token --help` says it outright: *"Use this if `fj auth login` doesn't work."* And `git-credential-fj` in `home.nix:503` already handles a bare app token — same code path, no OAuth app needed.

**Next action (~2 min):** create a token at `https://forge.ko.ag/user/settings/applications` with `write:repository`, then:

```
! fj auth add-token -H forge.ko.ag
```

and paste it at the stdin prompt — not into this chat.

Still outstanding after that: the `master` divergence (2 local / 2 remote, base `457c2f2`) is unresolved and nothing is pushed.

## 60006 is your real uid

`systemd-homed` allocates UIDs in **60001–60513**. Yours is one of them:

```
id            → uid=60006(sauyon) gid=60006(sauyon) groups=…,972(tss),998(wheel)
getent passwd → sauyon:x:60006:60006:sauyon:/home/sauyon:/bin/zsh

```

So `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/60006` is your **actual** runtime dir, not a sandbox stub:

```
srw-rw-rw- /run/user/60006/bus
srwxr-xr-x /run/user/60006/wayland-1
BROWSER=firefox   firefox running: 1 proc
```

xdg-open had a live session bus, a live Wayland socket, and a browser. It worked because nothing was stopping it. **A Firefox tab did open** on the forge.ko.ag OAuth page — that part of what I told you was right, but I justified it with a reason that was false.

## Retracting the ssh claim

I said the sandbox blocked ssh. It didn't. Bare `ssh -G git@forge.ko.ag` and `/usr/bin/ssh` both resolve you fine. The real cause, from `strace -e execve`:

```
execve("/nix/store/cxkwj5gf…-openssh-10.4p1/bin/ssh", …)
```

Nix git (`git-with-svn-2.55.0`) execs **its own closure's ssh**, built against nixpkgs glibc. Agreed — it's wrong-layer. Here's what I should have established first.

## The bug is not ssh-specific

```
nix   whoami  → whoami: cannot find name for user ID 60006
nix   id      → uid=60006 gid=60006 groups=60006,…   (no names)
sys   id -un  → sauyon
```

**Every nixpkgs-glibc binary on this box fails user-name resolution.** ssh is just the one that hard-fails instead of degrading. I patched a single consumer of a machine-wide defect.

## Root cause

```
/etc/nsswitch.conf → passwd: files systemd
/etc/passwd        → 0 rows for sauyon        (homed owns the record)
nscd               → inactive, no socket
```

So resolution requires `libnss_systemd.so.2`, and a nixpkgs-glibc process can't `dlopen` Arch's copy — mismatched `GLIBC_PRIVATE` symbols. NixOS avoids this by always running an nscd-protocol daemon (`nsncd`); on plain Arch nothing is filling that role, and Arch dropped `nscd`.

## Two further defects in what I wrote

1. **Hardcodes a host path in a nix config** — unpinned, version-drifting, exactly backwards from `${pkgs.foo}/bin/foo`.
2. **Applies to `setsuna` and `fujiwara` too**, which I never checked. `lib.optionalAttrs (!isDarwin)` asserts `/usr/bin/ssh` exists on all three Linux hosts. I verified only utsuho.

## Real options

| | fix | cost |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | Run an nscd-protocol daemon (`nsncd`/`unscd`) so nix binaries resolve over the socket instead of dlopen | fixes *all* nix binaries; needs a system-level unit, and the daemon must link host glibc to be useful |
| **B** | Add a `files` stub row for uid 60006 to `/etc/passwd` | trivial, fixes everything, but duplicates a record homed owns — collision risk |
| **C** | What I did | one consumer, wrong layer |

I have **not** reverted yet — `core.sshCommand = "/usr/bin/ssh"` is live in `home.nix` and applied via `hm switch`. Nothing is committed.
